title: Readwise Pricing: Plans and Costs (2026 Guide)
summary: Readwise pricing includes free and paid options with different feature sets and limits. Determine which tier provides the storage and tools you need.
body_markdown:
## Move Readwise highlights between apps with Activepieces


Check whether Readwise's own exports already do the job before you build anything; Activepieces can carry new Readwise highlights into another app, drawing on 746 integrations, and its free plan includes unlimited flows.


A workflow you maintain is a second system that can break quietly, so it has to earn its place.


### What Readwise already exports natively


Open Readwise's integrations and export settings first. Readwise has its own connections to several note-taking tools and exports your highlights as a file.


If your destination is one of those tools, the native route is the better default. It's maintained by the vendor, and when it fails you have one place to look instead of two.


That also protects the exit route the previous section described, because a native export is the one you can count on when you leave.


Only when the destination isn't covered is Activepieces worth the extra layer. It's also worth it when you want a highlight to land somewhere specific, such as a row in a database you already use for reading notes.


If your destination isn't on Readwise's native list, you wait until the vendor decides it's worth adding, because a closed catalogue grows on its owner's priorities.


Activepieces lets you generate the missing integration with AI and add it privately to your own instance, with no vendor release in the way.


Its 746 integrations are counted straight from the` packages/pieces/community` directory of the MIT-licensed GitHub monorepo, and roughly 60% of them were contributed by the community, which means most integrations lack official maintenance.


### One workflow worth building


Build one flow: when a new highlight appears, add a row to a notes database. The screenshot shows the builder with a Schedule trigger set to "Every Hour" selected.


The integration selector's open on spreadsheet apps such as Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel 365, with Insert Row among the available actions. Read it as a pattern, not a recipe.


Because the flow polls on a schedule, highlights arrive in batches rather than instantly, which is fine for a reading habit that doesn't need real-time delivery.


The panel on the right also shows a "Generate Sample Data" test that succeeded, and that step is where you confirm the trigger returns real data before trusting the flow.


Before you commit, open the Readwise integration in the selector and confirm it exposes the trigger or action you need. If it doesn't, the flow can't be built the way described here, and the native export remains your answer.
